docs.title: Phi-Genesis Research Programmes
docs.text: Purpose: a source-linked index of the distinct research programmes within the spectral audit. The sections identify research scope and evidence boundaries; they do not certify a physical interpretation.

docs.title: Spectral decimation and gap structure
docs.text:
The project examines the factor-five spectral-decimation structure and Fukushima–Shima gaps on finite Sierpiński-gasket graphs. Results must be interpreted with the documented corner-defect correction for the corner-degree-2 graph Laplacian.

See Verified Results and Computational Architecture.

docs.title: Boundary conditions and flux
docs.text:
Möbius and \(\pi\)-flux configurations are used to test how boundary conditions affect spectral gaps. A gap in a tested configuration is not evidence that the target indices \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) have been independently selected.

See Verified Results.

docs.title: Spectral counting and exponent estimation
docs.text:
The theoretical reference is \(d_s/2=\ln 3/\ln 5\). Finite-level estimates show window-dependent spread; Open Problem #2 remains open.

See Open Problems.

docs.title: Target-index selection audit
docs.text:
The preregistered tests did not meet the decision threshold. The proposed relation \(m=A n\) remains a fitted relation, not an independent prediction.

See Selection Protocol, Preregistration, and Protocol Ledger.

docs.title: Scientific boundary
docs.text:
The target indices \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) have not been independently derived from a spectral invariant. The relation \(m=A n\) is a fit, not an independent prediction. The claimed \(\eta\)-invariant value \(-4\) was not reproduced in the documented tests. Open Problem #2 remains open. None of these statuses is changed by the documentation architecture or a successful CI run.

docs.title: Verification layers
docs.text:
The project combines unit tests, numerical cross-checks and preregistered statistical tests. These answer different questions:

  • A unit test checks a specific implementation property.
  • A dense-spectrum comparison checks a numerical path against a smaller reference instance.
  • A preregistered null test evaluates whether a search result exceeds the specified chance baseline.
  • A theoretical derivation is needed for a general mathematical statement.

Passing one layer does not automatically establish claims that belong to another.

docs.title: Data, Provenance and Research Records
docs.text: Phi-Genesis maintains a distinction between source code, committed numerical artifacts, protocol commitments and later interpretation. This separation is essential because the research includes negative findings and reassessments of earlier apparent matches.

docs.title: Authoritative record hierarchy
docs.text:
1. Preregistration — the question, target set, rule, null ensembles, parameters and decision threshold fixed before evaluation.
  2. Code and data — the implementation, seeds, null pools and numerical outputs used in the test.
  3. Protocol ledger — the cumulative account of tested configurations, including exploratory and abandoned branches.
  4. Methodology — explanation of the statistical reasoning and interpretation limits.
  5. README and changelog — project-level summary and version history.
  6. Website and interactive portal — navigational and explanatory views, subordinate to the primary records.

docs.title: Current documented record
docs.text:
The current public project status is v2.2.1. The cumulative protocol ledger records 193 main-family configuration evaluations and an earlier carpet search of about 128 level-3 configurations plus an unrecorded level-4 sweep. Therefore the honest cumulative count is at least about 321, not a falsely precise total.

The carpet branch is marked abandoned after a null analysis reassessed its initial 4/4 match as consistent with a look-elsewhere effect. Protocol v1.0's power limitation is also explicitly documented; it is not treated as an informative negative.

docs.title: Provenance and limitations
docs.text:
• Do not present the four target indices as independently derived from the spectral operator.
  • Do not treat all target hits as equally informative: the base-rate audit found index 1 to be common under the tested ratio rule.
  • Do not describe the η-invariant value −4 as reproduced; the documented tests did not observe it.
  • Do not transfer the Lean verification status of Evgeny's Theorem to the separate Phi-Genesis computations.
  • Report finite graph level, operator convention, boundary conditions, estimator and numerical range with quantitative claims.

docs.title: Research Dissertation
docs.text:
Recursive Graph Operators, Spectral Trace Defects, and Higher-Moment Recurrence

Bibliographic field Record Author Evgeny Zaprudnov Research group RFT-SIRM Version 1.0 Date shown in the source 15 October 2026 Canonical manuscript DISSERTATION.md Source repository Evgeny's Theory of Everything

!!! info "Why the complete manuscript stays in its original repository" The dissertation contains mathematical notation, formulas, proof boundaries, finite-level certificates, numerical tables, and references. Linking to the canonical source avoids maintaining a second, potentially divergent copy inside Phi-Genesis. This page provides context and direct navigation; it is not a replacement manuscript.

docs.title: What the dissertation covers
docs.text: Strand Subject Evidence boundary Recursive graph operators Graph approximations and operator constructions on the Sierpiński gasket Definitions and results are scoped to the stated construction Fourth-moment trace defect A concrete identity for a specified SU(2)-connected operator The source project reports a Lean 4 formalization for the concrete proposition Higher even moments \(H^6\), \(H^8\), and \(H^{10}\) coefficient/recurrence research Finite-level certificates and numerical holdouts are not the same as an all-level proof Signed-flux spectral work \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-flux, spectral decimation, and boundary/corner corrections This is a distinct operator programme; Gate A and the mass-index rule remain open in Phi-Genesis Research methodology Reproducibility, explicit exceptions, numerical holdouts, and open problems Claims must be interpreted at the evidence level recorded in the source

docs.title: A mathematical anchor: the fourth-moment identity
docs.text:
The theorem repository states the following identity for its specified operators and assumptions:

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) =\operatorname{Tr}(H_C^4)-\operatorname{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right)\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\ge1. \]

The normalized quantity is defined as

\[ I_m(\theta)=\frac{\Delta_m(H^4,\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3}, \qquad \lim_{m\to\infty}I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

At \(\theta=\pi/2\), the limiting value is \(-8/9\).

!!! warning "Scope of the theorem" The formula above belongs to the concrete fourth-moment proposition in the Evgeny-Theorem source repository. It does not, by itself, establish the higher-moment all-level recurrence, close Phi-Genesis Gate A, derive the indices \(\{1,12,17,40\}\), prove a physical mass law, or establish a complete physical Theory of Everything.

docs.title: How this relates to Phi-Genesis
docs.text:
The two projects are related research strands, but they use different mathematical objects and answer different questions.

Evgeny-Theorem / dissertation strand Phi-Genesis strand Operator focus A specified SU(2)-connected graph operator Signed \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-flux / \(\pi\)-flux Laplacians Main observable Fourth-moment trace defect and related higher-moment questions Low-lying spectrum, gaps, decimation, and candidate mass indices Strongest stated evidence A concrete fourth-moment Lean formalization; finite-level higher-moment certificates and holdouts Reproducible numerical checks and preregistered selection searches Key unresolved question Proving the proposed higher-moment recurrence for all stated levels/angles from the recursive structure Characterizing the full decimation exceptional set and deriving target indices independently Does one establish the other? No No

A formal proof in one repository does not transfer automatically to another operator, observable, or physical interpretation. A bridge between these constructions would need its own definitions, assumptions, derivation, and verification.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This page records the role of finite-level experiments in the Phi-Genesis research programme. They are computational checks on specified graph families and parameter choices, not physical-device experiments.

docs.title: Evidence summary
docs.text:
• Spectral-decimation and gap patterns are reproduced numerically within the documented scope.
  • Finite-level spectral-exponent estimates vary with the counting window and estimator.
  • Preregistered target-selection tests did not meet the required threshold.
  • The claimed \(\eta\)-invariant value \(-4\) was not reproduced in the documented tests.

docs.title: Reporting requirements
docs.text:
Every reported trial should identify the graph level, number of vertices, operator and boundary convention, algorithm, precision, parameters, and any failed or excluded cases.

docs.title: Independent Verification and Test Boundaries
docs.text: Phi-Genesis is a spectral-computation project and does not claim to perform seL4 kernel verification. This page documents the analogous evidence boundary: computational tests validate only the specified implementation, operator, configuration, and parameter range.

docs.title: What a test can support
docs.text:
• Reproduction of a finite numerical observation.
  • Detection of implementation errors covered by the test.
  • A documented negative result for the tested family and decision rule.

docs.title: What it cannot support by itself
docs.text:
• An all-level mathematical theorem.
  • A physical mass-generation mechanism.
  • An independent selection rule for \(\{1,12,17,40\}\).
  • A claim about software or hardware systems not tested by the project.

For the actual computational methods and results, see Verified Results and Computational Architecture.

docs.title: Spectral anchor
docs.text:
For the Sierpiński gasket, the theoretical spectral exponent is

\[ \frac{d_s}{2}=\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 5}\approx 0.6826. \]

The factor-five scaling is a reference structure for finite-level spectral-decimation experiments. The corner-degree-2 graph Laplacian requires the documented corner-defect corrections.

docs.title: Boundary conditions
docs.text: Möbius and \(\pi\)-flux variants test how boundary conditions alter finite graph spectra and gap structure. Observing a gap does not identify a unique mass index or establish a physical mechanism.

docs.title: Evidence vocabulary
docs.text:
The project distinguishes numerical reproduction, preregistered statistical outcomes, fitted relationships, and open conjectures. A fitted relationship \(m=A n\) is not an independently derived prediction; the target set \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) remains unselected by an established invariant.

See Verified Results, Glossary, and Open Problems.

docs.title: Spectral decimation
docs.text: A recursive relation connecting spectral data at successive graph approximations. In this project, the principal scaling factor is approximately five, with corrections for the corner-degree-2 Laplacian.

docs.title: Sierpiński gasket (SG)
docs.text: The self-similar graph used as the main spectral substrate for the documented computations.

docs.title: Spectral dimension
docs.text: The exponent associated with spectral counting. For the Sierpiński gasket, the theoretical value used here is \(d_s/2=\ln 3/\ln 5\approx0.6826\).

docs.title: Fukushima–Shima gaps
docs.text: Forbidden spectral intervals associated with the spectral-decimation structure. The repository reports their finite-level numerical reproduction within the documented setup.

docs.title: Möbius / \(\pi\)-flux boundary condition
docs.text: A boundary twist used to study how flux changes the graph spectrum. The tested full \(\pi\)-flux configuration opens a gap, but this does not establish the target mass-index rule.

docs.title: Target indices
docs.text: The four integers \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) used in the proposed mass relation. Their independent derivation from a spectral invariant has not been established.

docs.title: Look-elsewhere effect
docs.text: The statistical inflation of apparent significance when many configurations, rules, or parameter choices are tested. Phi-Genesis records configuration counts and preregistered decision thresholds to make this risk explicit.

docs.title: Null-only power check
docs.text: A check, designed without looking at target outcomes, that establishes whether a protocol could reach its decision threshold under an idealized target-compatible result.

docs.title: Inertia count
docs.text: The number of eigenvalues below a chosen threshold, computed from the inertia of a shifted matrix. The project's sparse-LU method is numerical and floating-point based, not a machine-checked proof.

docs.title: Evidence labels
docs.text:
• Reproduced numerically: observed again with documented computation and scope.
  • No evidence: the tested protocol did not meet its predeclared threshold.
  • Not reproduced: a prior claim was not obtained in the documented tests.
  • Open: current evidence does not settle the question.
  • Fit, not prediction: parameters or target indices were chosen using the data being matched.

docs.title: Methodology — Testing Spectral Selection Rules
docs.text: This page explains the method used to test whether spectral configurations select the target indices \(T=\{1,12,17,40\}\). The full versioned protocol is maintained in METHODOLOGY.md; the cumulative record is the protocol ledger.

docs.title: The question and the look-elsewhere effect
docs.text:
The mass formula \(m=A n\) fits four selected masses with one scale and four integer indices. The central research question is not whether the fit can be written down, but whether a spectral rule independently selects those indices. Trying many operator configurations makes accidental matches increasingly likely.

The protocol therefore asks whether a configuration scores unusually well relative to null ensembles after taking the maximum over the tested configurations. A striking individual match is not enough.

docs.title: Protocol design
docs.text:
1. Fix the target and rule. Record the target set, index-selection rule, spectral window and tested family before evaluation.
  2. Define null ensembles. Use generic operators of the relevant type to estimate how often each target appears by chance.
  3. Weight by base rate. Common targets should contribute less evidence than rare targets.
  4. Correct for searching many configurations. The test statistic uses the best score across the family, not just a hand-picked configuration.
  5. Check power using null data alone. Confirm that the chosen statistic and threshold can be reached before evaluating the target family.
  6. Use a fixed decision threshold. A candidate must reach \(p\le0.01\) under both specified null ensembles.
  7. Keep a cumulative ledger. Record abandoned, exploratory and related families, and disclose dependence between them.

docs.title: Why the power check matters
docs.text: Protocol v1.0 was unable to reach the decision threshold even if a configuration selected all four targets. Its negative outcome therefore did not meaningfully discriminate the tested family. Later protocols changed \(k\) using null-only design so that the threshold could be reached. Those later tests still did not pass.

docs.title: Interpretation discipline
docs.text: A negative result applies to the tested family, selection rule, parameter range and null model. It does not prove that no mechanism can exist. Conversely, a numerical match after choosing targets and trying many configurations is not a prediction.

docs.title: Open Problems and Research Roadmap
docs.text: This page distinguishes unresolved research questions from completed diagnostics. The current documented release is v2.2.1. Items below are not presented as solved.

docs.title: 1. Independent selection rule for the mass indices
docs.text:
Question. Can an operator or boundary-condition invariant select \(n\in\{1,12,17,40\}\) independently of the masses used to identify the target set?

Current status. No selection rule has been found in the tested families. Protocol versions v1.1 and v1.2.1 were designed so that the decision threshold was reachable, but neither passed the criterion. The earlier v1.0 test could not reach the threshold even in its best possible case and is therefore not an informative negative.

Work already recorded. Generation twists, scalar vertex potentials and corner Dirichlet conditions, SG × S¹ with lattice and continuum circles, and a Sierpiński-carpet search. The carpet's initial apparent 4/4 match was reassessed against chance and the branch was abandoned.

What would justify reopening the search. A new operator family with an a-priori mathematical rationale, a new preregistration, null-only power analysis, and an explicit accounting of all previous configuration families. A derivation of the indices from an operator invariant would be stronger than another post-hoc match.

See the selection-protocol audit.

docs.title: 2. Finite-level convergence of the spectral exponent
docs.text:
Question. Can a finite-level estimator recover the asymptotic spectral exponent robustly without depending materially on a chosen log-periodic window?

The theoretical value is \(d_s/2=\ln3/\ln5\approx0.6826\). Ordinary regression fits show finite-level and window bias. The repository reports that the level-9 chord estimator is within 0.1% of its stated comparison expression for \(N\ge1000\), while sliding-window fits still vary with window width and phase. These are not contradictory: one is a specific estimator result, while the broader robustness and convergence question remains open.

Documented inertia counts. Sparse-LU inertia computations reach level 10 (88,575 vertices). For the stated fixed three-log-period window, the reported exponent deviations are −2.19% (level 6), −0.61% (level 7), +0.07% (level 8), +0.32% (level 9) and +0.41% (level 10). A level-9 sliding-window study still shows dependence on window width. Level 11 and above have not been tested in the documented run.

Path forward. Derive an analytical finite-size correction from decimation theory or establish an estimator whose output is stable under reasonable window choices. More levels alone are not expected to remove estimator-window dependence.

See reproducibility instructions and the source scripts in protocol_data.

docs.title: 3. Light fermions and a physical bridge
docs.text:
Question. Can the research define a model that addresses light fermions and independently connects the fitted scale to the electroweak scale?

The repository does not currently define a Lagrangian or beta functions for the proposed bridge, so an RG calculation is not yet specified. A toy NJL-type equation would introduce its own coupling and cutoff; these parameters must be counted against the number of masses explained. These items remain blocked until a concrete model is stated.

docs.title: Research discipline for the next phase
docs.text:
1. State the mathematical rationale before testing a new family.
  2. Freeze the rule, null pools, statistic and decision threshold before evaluating targets.
  3. Check power from null draws alone.
  4. Count abandoned and exploratory searches in the cumulative ledger.
  5. Label post-hoc analyses and dependencies between related operator families.
  6. Keep a negative result bounded to the tested family and parameter range.

See Methodology, Protocol Ledger, and Changelog.

docs.title: Origin Chronology
docs.text: This page records the documented research sequence without inventing dates or implying that later work validates earlier hypotheses.

docs.title: Research trail
docs.text:
1. Spectral observations on gasket-like graph families. Initial numerical patterns motivated questions about decimation, gaps, and target indices.
  2. Broader family searches. Additional operator and configuration families were examined; the growing search space made the look-elsewhere effect central to interpretation.
  3. Preregistered tests. The selection hypothesis was tested with declared thresholds and null models. The documented tests did not meet the required threshold.
  4. Methodology correction. Underpowered designs and post-selection risks were explicitly recorded rather than treated as positive evidence.
  5. Current status — v2.2.1. The project reports bounded numerical observations, a still-open finite-window exponent question, and no independently established target-index rule.

docs.title: Reproducibility and Computational Workflow
docs.text: The repository's source code, tests, fixed-seed protocol data and versioned records are the primary reproducibility artifacts. This guide summarizes the commands in the project README; use a clean local clone and follow the cautions below.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
The project uses Python with NumPy and SciPy for numerical work.

pip install numpy scipy
python -c "import phi_genesis; print('OK')"

For editable installation and tests:

pip install -e . pytest
pytest -q -m "not nightly"

The README reports that the fast suite can take roughly 2–3 minutes on one CPU core, with the level-8 test dominating. Nightly tests are excluded by this command.

docs.title: Reproduce protocol v1.2.1
docs.text:
python -m phi_genesis.selection_protocol_v121 stepA
python -m phi_genesis.selection_protocol_v121 stepB
  • stepA regenerates the null pools using seeds fixed in the code; the README estimates about 15 minutes.
  • stepB runs the evaluation and should be compared with protocol_data/results_v1_2_1.json.
  • Caution: stepA rewrites protocol_data/null_pools_v1_2_1.json. If you want to preserve the committed file exactly, perform the reproduction on a separate working copy.

docs.title: Reproduce Open Problem #2 estimator studies
docs.text:
python protocol_data/op2_window_bias.py table
python protocol_data/op2_window_bias.py sliding
python protocol_data/op2_chord_estimator.py 8 9

The window-bias script uses the cached numerical inertia counts documented by the project. The chord-estimator command compares levels 8 and 9 for the documented estimator.

docs.title: What to record
docs.text:
For a reproducible report, include:

  • Git commit SHA and Python / NumPy / SciPy versions;
  • exact command and test selection;
  • graph level, operator convention, boundary condition and numerical tolerance;
  • protocol version, random seeds and null ensemble;
  • whether an output was regenerated or read from committed data;
  • any deviation from preregistered settings.

A passing test suite validates the tested code paths, not every scientific interpretation in the repository. Numerical results should always be reported with their level, estimator, parameter range and known limitations.

docs.title: Phi-Genesis — Spectral Research Home
docs.text:
Sierpiński-gasket spectral structure, boundary-condition experiments, reproducible computation, and evidence-bounded research.

🟢 FEATURED RESEARCH RECORD

Spectral decimation, corner-defect corrections, and the target-index selection audit

Phi-Genesis separates numerically reproduced spectral structure, finite-level estimates, preregistered tests, and open conjectures. The research record does not establish an independent spectral rule selecting the target indices \(\{1,12,17,40\}\), and it does not claim a completed physical mass-generation mechanism.

Phi-Genesis is the RFT-SIRM spectral research programme for the Sierpiński gasket. Begin with the research map and the boundaries of the available evidence; then inspect the results, selection protocol, computational methods, and chronology. The versioned source records remain authoritative.

  • Research map — follow the evidence
  • Verified spectral results and limitations
  • Selection protocol and negative results
  • Interactive spectral research portal
  • Research history and chronology
  • Project README and source repository

Scope: Phi-Genesis is a numerical spectral audit. Its findings do not inherit the Lean proof status of the separate Evgeny-Theorem repository. A reproduced finite-level observation, a statistical test, a fitted relation, and a mathematical theorem are different evidence classes.

docs.title: Research map
docs.text: Use the Research Map to navigate the research hierarchy, spectral anchor, evidence labels, and unresolved questions. The map is organized by research relationship and evidence status, not by an implied claim that every downstream hypothesis follows from the spectral observations.

docs.title: The mathematical anchor
docs.text:
For the Sierpiński gasket, the theoretical spectral exponent is

\[ \frac{d_s}{2}=\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 5}\approx 0.6826. \]

The factor-five spectral-decimation structure and Fukushima–Shima gap structure are reproduced numerically within the documented finite-level scope, with corner-defect corrections for the corner-degree-2 graph Laplacian. Finite-window estimates remain sensitive to the counting window and estimator; the known exponent is a consistency reference, not a new prediction.

The proposed mass relation

\[ m=A n \]

uses a fitted scale and the target indices \(\{1,12,17,40\}\). Those indices have not been independently derived from a spectral invariant. The relation is a fit, not a prediction.

docs.title: Selected results and limits
docs.text:
• Spectral decimation: eigenvalues scale by approximately a factor of five between levels, subject to the documented corner-defect correction.
  • Weyl exponent: \(d_s/2=\ln 3/\ln 5\) is the theoretical value; finite-window estimates show phase-dependent spread.
  • Boundary twists: the tested full \(\pi\)-flux configuration opens a spectral gap, but this does not select all four target indices.
  • Selection audit: preregistered tests v1.0, v1.1, and v1.2.1 did not meet the required threshold. Version v1.0 was underpowered; v1.1 and v1.2.1 could reach the threshold but did not.
  • \(\eta\)-invariant: the previously claimed value \(-4\) was not reproduced in the documented tests.
  • Top-quark index: candidates 1654, 1664, and 1680 remain inconsistent under the documented scale choices; no candidate is asserted as correct.

These are bounded findings about tested operators, configurations, methods, and parameter ranges. They do not establish a physical mass-generation mechanism.

docs.title: Research question
docs.text:
Does any tested operator family on Sierpiński-gasket graph approximations select the target indices \(T=\{1,12,17,40\}\) more often than expected by chance, after accounting for the number of configurations tried?

The target indices were identified from a mass fit; therefore a match is not independent evidence by itself. The selection search uses a look-elsewhere correction over the configurations within each family, null ensembles, target weights based on null base rates, and a predeclared decision threshold of \(p\le0.01\) in both null ensembles.

docs.title: Preregistered results
docs.text:
Protocol Family / rule Configurations Result Power status v1.0 F1 + F2 + F3; \(k=12\), window 60 75 No evidence; p = 0.922 / 0.968 Threshold unreachable; negative is uninformative about whether the family contains a rule. v1.1 Same family; \(k=6\), window 60 75 No evidence; p = 0.966 / 0.997 Threshold reachable; informative negative for these configurations. v1.2.1 SG × S¹ continuum circle, two spin structures; \(k=8\), window 60 10 No evidence; p = 0.953 / 0.926 Threshold reachable; informative negative for these configurations.

The p-value pairs are ordered as documented in the source records (N-pot / N-edge for v1.0 and v1.1; N-circ / N-circpot for v1.2.1). Each pair fails the requirement that both nulls meet the threshold.

The cumulative ledger records 193 configuration evaluations from the documented main families, plus an earlier Sierpiński-carpet search of about 128 level-3 configurations and an unrecorded level-4 sweep. The honest cumulative statement is therefore at least about 321, not an exact exhaustive count.

docs.title: Other relevant checks
docs.text:
• Generation twists: all 32 \(2^5\) configurations at level 5 were tested; maximum target overlap was 1 of 4, and index 40 was never selected.
  • Base-rate audit: under random on-site potentials, the ratio-based rule selected index 1 about 95% of the time, while index 40 appeared about 3.4% of the time. Hits on the four indices are therefore not equally informative.
  • Carpet branch: the early 4/4 match was reassessed against a null model; the record attributes it to a look-elsewhere effect and marks that branch abandoned.
  • v1.0 power correction: even a configuration selecting all four targets would not have reached the required p-value. This was documented as a limitation of that protocol rather than treated as evidence against all possible mechanisms.

docs.title: What the result means
docs.text:
The tested families did not satisfy the preregistered selection criterion. This is a bounded negative result: it does not prove that no operator family could select the indices. It does mean the current mass formula cannot be described as a spectral prediction.

Any new family must have an a-priori rationale and a new preregistration, with null-only power design completed before target evaluation. Re-running the same search on the same four targets would increase the look-elsewhere burden rather than resolve it.

docs.title: Research Strategy
docs.text: The next research phase should prioritize closure conditions and reproducibility over expanding the number of exploratory searches.

docs.title: Priorities
docs.text:
1. Resolve the window dependence of finite-level spectral-exponent estimates with a declared estimator and uncertainty analysis.
  2. Specify a mathematically independent candidate rule for the target indices before evaluating new data.
  3. Design null-only power checks that can reach the declared decision threshold.
  4. Record every tested family, exclusions, parameter choices, and stopping rule.
  5. Preserve negative outcomes and distinguish numerical evidence from theorem-level conclusions.

docs.title: Release discipline
docs.text:
No new selection claim should be promoted unless the rule is independently specified, its test is adequately powered, and the result survives the declared multiple-testing and dependence controls.

docs.title: Verified Results and Evidence Boundaries
docs.text: This page summarises the results recorded in Phi-Genesis v2.2.1. “Verified” here means supported by the stated derivation, numerical computation or regression test within its stated scope. It does not mean that every claim is machine-checked or that finite-level evidence proves a universal theorem.

docs.title: 1. Sierpiński-gasket spectral structure
docs.text:
• Spectral decimation: the characteristic eigenvalue scale factor is 5 between consecutive levels, with corner-defect corrections for the corner-degree-2 Laplacian used in this repository.
  • Fukushima–Shima gaps: the computations recover forbidden zones associated with fixed points near \(\lambda\approx2.5\) and \(\lambda\approx3\).
  • Log-periodic structure: the counting data exhibit the expected periodic signature associated with the factor-5 scaling.

These statements concern the graph family, operator convention and finite-level checks documented in the source. Start with source code and the README.

docs.title: 2. Weyl exponent and finite-level estimates
docs.text:
For the Sierpiński gasket, the theoretical exponent is

\[ \frac{d_s}{2}=\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 5}\approx0.6826. \]

The repository reports that a window-free chord estimator is within 0.1% of its stated comparison expression at level 9 for \(N\ge1000\). This is a result for that estimator and range, not proof that every finite-level estimator converges uniformly.

The inertia-based count path uses Sylvester's law of inertia with sparse LU rather than computing the full spectrum. The documented level-10 graph has 88,575 vertices. The reported resource figures and window studies are implementation- and parameter-specific; see Open Problem #2 and the reproduction guide.

docs.title: 3. Möbius / π-flux boundary conditions
docs.text:
For the tested level-5 graph, the documented full π-flux configuration raises the first eigenvalue from approximately 0.006 to approximately 0.46, opening a spectral gap in that instance. Partial twists also produce gaps in the tested cases.

This does not establish a selection mechanism for \(\{1,12,17,40\}\). In the exhaustive search of all \(2^5=32\) generation-twist configurations, the maximum simultaneous target hit was 1 of 4 and index 40 was never selected.

docs.title: 4. Integer mass fit — a fit, not a prediction
docs.text:
The repository records a single-scale fit \(m=A n\), with \(A=104.63\) MeV and integer indices \(n=\{1,12,17,40\}\), matching four selected masses with a mean error of about 0.68%.

The index set was chosen with the masses in view. Because no independent spectral rule has derived those indices, this numerical agreement is not a prediction and must not be described as a confirmed mass law. The alternative scale expression documented in the README gives approximately 100.13 MeV, about 4.3% below the fitted value.

The top-quark index is unresolved: the repository documents candidates 1654, 1664 and 1680 arising from different procedures/scales. No single candidate is endorsed.

docs.title: 5. η-invariant claim — not reproduced
docs.text: The RFT-String v8.7 claim \(\bar\eta(0)=-4\) for the stated boundary potential was not reproduced. The documented test reports asymmetry +1 for the claimed potential, −1 for a random potential, and −2 for zero potential; −4 was not observed in the tested cases. The repository interprets the observed asymmetry as a finite-size effect, not as a demonstrated topological invariant.

docs.title: 6. How to read the evidence
docs.text:
Label Interpretation Theoretical identity Follows from specified mathematical definitions and assumptions. Reproducible numerical result A computation can be rerun for the documented finite instance and implementation. Fit / estimator output Depends on model choice, parameter range and estimator design. Negative search result The tested family did not meet its predeclared criterion; it does not prove no mechanism exists anywhere. Open problem Current evidence is incomplete, inconclusive, or sensitive to a remaining methodological choice.

Phi-Genesis' numerical results are not automatically formal proofs. In particular, the Lean-verified status of Evgeny's Theorem does not transfer to this repository: the operator families, observables and verification methods differ.
